newsitem.title: FRANCE: European Parliament backs EU broadcast rules.
newsitem.headline: European Parliament backs EU broadcast rules.

text.p: The European Parliament gave final approval Tuesday to new European Union broadcasting legislation, which will leave Hollywood's domination of the bloc's television screens unchallenged.

The revised television without frontiers law, expected to cross its final hurdle when EU culture ministers meet in Luxembourg on June 30, will also guarantee European viewers can see major sporting events when exclusive rights are snapped up by pay television channels.
The process of revising the 1989 law lasted more than two years, as France and Euro-MPs fought with EU governments in vain for stricter limits on the number of Hollywood films and sitcoms.
"Sadly we missed a great opportunity to create a level playing field in the audiovisual sector," said British Socialist deputy Carole Tongue.
The Parliament, however, was able to secure rules forcing EU countries to respect each others' lists of major sporting events which must be shown free.
